map.NATO/ICAO 音标字母表：A–Z 各对应一个易辨识单词（Alfa、Brav: NATO/ICAO phonetic alphabet: each of A–Z maps to an easily distinguished word (Alfa, Bravo, Charlie…), and 0–9 are read as Zero…Nine (radio practice reads 9 as Niner); this page converts letters and digits only and passes other characters through unchanged.
map.NATO/ICAO 音标字母表给 A–Z 各配一个易辨识单词，用于电话、无线电、: The NATO/ICAO phonetic alphabet assigns each of A–Z an easily distinguished word for telephone, radio, callsign and coordinate dictation, avoiding confusion between similar-sounding letters such as B/P, D/T and M/N. The official spellings are Alfa (not Alpha) and Juliett (not Juliet). Digits 0–9 are read Zero, One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, Seven, Eight, Nine; in radio practice 9 is often read Niner to avoid confusion with German nein and similar words, and the third column on this page also gives NINER. The page converts A–Z and 0–9 only, keeps spaces and passes other characters through unchanged.
